subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: When Fines Don't Work
description: A quick win: understand When Fines Don't Work.

hook.text: Facebook was fined $5 billion by the FTC. Its stock price went up the same day.

buildup.text: Regulators fine companies for privacy violations, but the fines are often a fraction of revenue.

discovery.text: Google's largest GDPR fine was $57 million — less than what it earns in five hours.

twist.text: If fines are cheaper than compliance, companies treat them as a cost of doing business.

climax.text: When the penalty is less than the profit, it's not a fine — it's a fee for violating your privacy.

punchline.text: Fined billions. Still profitable. Nothing changed.

quiz.question: Why do large privacy fines often fail to change corporate behavior?
options: The fines are often a tiny fraction of company revenue
Fines are paid by the government, not the company
